items.headline: ETRM shadow spreadsheets persist despite system upgrades
items.summary: A CTRM Center analysis argues traders keep parallel Excel sheets not due to weak engines but fragile data chains, including failed price uploads and late trade bookings. The piece frames shadow books as a governance and transparency gap, not a technology one.

items.headline: UK court upholds 'pay when paid' LC clause
items.summary: Per GTR, a UK court ruled in favour of Euro Exim Bank's letter of credit clause making payment conditional on the issuing bank itself being paid, a notable precedent for structuring LC risk in commodity deals.

items.headline: Port congestion ties up global container capacity
items.summary: C.H. Robinson reported that port congestion, vessel bunching and Golden Week sailings are straining schedule reliability, with Trans-Pacific capacity cuts and continued Hormuz and Panama disruptions complicating Q4 freight planning.

items.headline: Suez Canal transits climb as carriers return
items.summary: Drewry data show Suez Canal transits in week 39 running 68% higher year-on-year as more carriers resume the route, adding capacity to Asia-Europe trade even as Red Sea security concerns persist.
